action: Place scanner in the sagittal plane.
Scan inferiorly through the pelvis. Evaluate the bladder volume.
interpretation: Note that the bladder is not full. Visualize the vagina and cervix despite the limited acoustic window.

action: Orient the probe midline on the uterus.
Scan back and forth through the uterus.
interpretation: Obtain an overall view of the uterine structure.
Establish the presence of a single pregnancy and only one fetus.

action: Scan low in the pelvis. Position the probe just behind the pubic bone.
interpretation: Identify the bladder located posterior to the pubic bone.
Move the field of view up from the bladder.

action: Direct the beam towards the right adnexa.
interpretation: Visualize the right ovary. Identify a possible corpus luteum cyst.

action: Scan superiorly through the extent of the pelvis.
interpretation: Confirm definitively that there is only one baby present.

action: Focus on the contents of the gestational sac. Zoom the image.
interpretation: Optimize resolution to inspect the sac contents.

action: Observe the echogenicity within the sac.
interpretation: Identify the black anechoic area as the fluid surrounding the baby.
Identify the embryo, distinguishing the head end and the rump end.
Visualize a tiny yolk sac. Confirm appearance is normal for this stage of pregnancy.

action: Inspect the sac for the amnion membrane.
interpretation: Assess for the amnion, noting that it may not be visible if fused at this point.
